channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Trades below 1.1400, near two-month low ahead of Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The EUR/USD pair drifts lower for the third straight day, hitting a fresh low since July 28 during the Asian session on Thursday, though it lacks follow-through.

item.title: Swiss Franc strengthens ahead of SNB policy decision
item.description: USD/CHF loses ground after registering modest gains the previous day, trading around 0.8240 during Asian hours on Thursday. Traders await the Swiss National Bank (SNB) interest rate decision due later in the day.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold steadies, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices remained broadly unchanged in India on Thursday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar consolidates around 0.5675 vs USD as bears await Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The NZD/USD pair flatlines around the 0.5675 region, trading just above its lowest level since early July, set the previous day, as investors await a meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Softens below 180.00, bearish bias persists below 100-day SMA
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross trades in negative territory around 179.85 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. Intervention risks from Japanese authorities provide some support to the Japanese Yen (JPY) against the Euro (EUR). Germany’s IFO survey is due later on Thursday.

item.title: Gold struggles below $4,300, one-week low as Fed hike bets and Iran risks underpin USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) touches a one-week low during the Asian session on Thursday, though it lacks follow-through as traders await a crucial meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.

item.title: Canadian Dollar holds steady amid oil uncertainties, hawkish Fed sentiment
item.description: USD/CAD steadies after three days of gains, trading around 1.4100 during Asian hours on Thursday. The USD/CAD pair has moved little as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) maintains its position amid cautious sentiment surrounding oil prices.

item.title: United States Dollar Index holds gains slightly above 101 amid strong US growth prospects
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) holds onto Wednesday’s strong gains in the Asian trade on Thursday. As of writing, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, trades firmly near a fresh eight week high of 101.23 posted the previous day.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $64.00 amid rising Fed rate hike odds
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around $64.10 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen gathers strength amid surging 10-year JGB yields
item.description: The USD/JPY pair attracts some sellers to around 157.85 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) as traders remain on high alert for further intervention from Japanese authorities.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines against Japanese Yen following mixed jobs data
item.description: AUD/JPY extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 110.80 during Asian hours on Thursday. The currency cross continues to trade under pressure as the Australian Dollar (AUD) remains subdued following the release of the latest domestic labor market data.

item.title: Australia’s Unemployment Rate rises to 4.6% in August, vs 4.5% expected
item.description: Australia’s Unemployment Rate climbed to 4.6% in August from 4.5% in July, according to the official data released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) on Thursday. The figure came in above the market consensus of 4.5%.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Principles on FX established since coordinated intervention remain in effect
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama said on Thursday that principles on foreign exchance established since coordinated Japan-US intervention remain in effect.

item.title: Australian Dollar hangs near August 7 low after weak jobs data, ahead of Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The AUD/USD pair hits a fresh low since August 7, around the 0.7025 region, following the release of Australian monthly jobs data, though it lacks follow-through selling and defends the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) pivotal support.

item.title: WTI slips below $91.00 despite rising US-Iran friction
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price depreciates after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $90.80 per barrel during Asian hours on Thursday. Crude oil prices may rebound as ongoing uncertainty surrounds the progress of the United States (US)-Iran diplomatic talks.

item.title: British Pound bears retain control near July lows amid Fed-BoE divergence
item.description: The GBP/USD pair sticks to a mildly negative bias for the fourth straight day, trading around the 1.3230-1.3225 region during the Asian session on Thursday, near its lowest level since early July, touched the previous day.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7489 vs. 6.7468 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Thursday at 6.7489 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7468 and 6.7184 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro weakens below 1.1400 as Fed rate hike expectations reinforce US Dollar strength
item.description: The EUR/USD pair loses ground to near 1.1380 during the early Asian trading hours on Thursday. The major pair extends its downside as hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve (Fed) boost the US Dollar (USD) against the Euro (EUR).

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says US-China trade truce extended through January 10
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the United States (US) and China have agreed to extend a bilateral trade truce that was set to expire in November through January 10, Blomoberg reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy says ready for energy ceasefire with Russia
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv remains ready for a bilateral “energy ceasefire” with Russia after holding separate talks with the leaders of the United States (US) and the United Kingdom (UK) in New York City, CNBC reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Iran President sends defiant message to US over potential talks
item.description: Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian said that the country won’t allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a US blockade remain in place, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar cools off against the New Zealand Dollar before jobs data
item.description: Tuesday's peak just under 1.2500 was the highest for AUD/NZD since early 2013. The cross is trading just above 1.2400, on track for a second straight down day.

item.title: Gold falls below $4,300 on Fed hawkish signals
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to near $4,290 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The precious metal loses momentum as hawkish signals from Federal Reserve (Fed) policymakers bolstered rate hike expectations, weighing on non-yielding bullion.

item.title: Australian Dollar tumbles amid soaring US yields, ahead of jobs data
item.description: The Aussie Dollar stumbles over 1% against the US Dollar on Wednesday as US Treasury yields soar, with the US 5- and 10-year T-note yields surpassing the 5% threshold amid investor confidence in further Federal Reserve tightening. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7039 after peaking at 0.7118.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slides toward its range floor as US yields climb
item.description: The bottom of NZD/USD's range since April is about 0.5600, and the pair is back in the lower part of it. It is trading just under 0.5700, its lowest since early July, which is about where it was before the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) began raising rates on July 8.

item.title: Japanese Yen gives back most of its rally as Fed hike talk grows
item.description: Holding up the Yen is costing Japan more each time and working for less time. USD/JPY is trading above 158.00, on track for its first daily close above its 200-day average since September 2.

item.title: Euro extends its slide as US surveys top Europe's strong reading
item.description: Europe's September business surveys were the strongest since April 2023, and the Euro fell to its lowest since late July on the day they came out. The eurozone's flash Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) composite reading came in at 53.1 against a 51.5 forecast, with services at 53 against 51.7.

item.title: British Pound sells off hard as US surveys outpace the UK's
item.description: Wednesday's flash Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) surveys showed US business growing at its fastest pace since July 2021 and British business slowing.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bears press 209.00 as downtrend deepens
item.description: The GBP/JPY pair extends its losses on Wednesday to two straight trading sessions, down over 0.17% and trading near the week's lows, with 209.40 seen as the first support level before sellers push prices lower.

item.title: Mexican Peso selloff deepens as Fed hawks drive USD/MXN toward 17.50
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) extends its depreciation against the Greenback as the USD/MXN pair rallies over 1.25% amid speculation that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise rates again, with Fed officials leaning hawkish and underpinning the US Dollar (USD).
